note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute swelling of the upper lip after eating a prawn soup (patient initially stated it was not a sandwich).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Ate prawn soup at approximately 7:00 PM.
  - Lip symptoms began within ~30 minutes and have been progressively worsening since onset.
  - Patient reports swelling feels like it is "getting bigger" and "pumping blood."
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat: sensation of not being able to breathe well; feeling of throat/chest closing.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: not reported.
  - Drooling: not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: not reported.
  - Dyspnea: subjective difficulty breathing and possible chest tightness.
  - Distribution of swelling: upper lip, started at left corner then involving upper lip.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Approximately 1 year ago: similar swelling after eating (suspected curry) with subsequent breathing difficulty; patient used salbutamol inhaler at that time (no other details documented).
  - Childhood: mother reports a severe allergic episode when patient was ~6 years old requiring unspecified injection/hospital care (patient uncertain of details).
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Known peanut allergy.
  - Asthma treated with salbutamol inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Uses antihistamines "sometimes" for peanut allergy but specific agent(s) not documented.
  - At initial part of visit patient did not have antihistamines available; later the mother reported having antihistamines (agent not specified).
- Any relevant social context:
  - Initially alone; a person (mother) arrived during consultation and stayed with patient.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - Patient reports visible swelling of the upper lip, beginning at left corner and increasing in size (self-reported).
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Patient reports subjective difficulty breathing and possible chest tightness; no objective stridor or noisy breathing documented.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Patient felt dizzy during the consultation.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient:
  - Mother arrived and was present during the consultation.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Suspected anaphylactic or evolving systemic allergic reaction after ingestion of prawn (seafood) in a patient with known peanut allergy and prior episodes of allergic swelling and breathing difficulty.
- Key justifications from transcript:
  - Temporal relationship: symptoms began within ~30 minutes of eating prawn soup.
  - Progressive lip swelling and new/worsening respiratory symptoms (subjective difficulty breathing, chest discomfort).
  - Past history of significant allergic reactions (childhood injection/hospitalization; similar episode ~1 year ago with breathing difficulty).
- Conflict noted:
  - Doctor initially stated they would call an ambulance, then subsequently instructed the mother to call emergency services (999). Both statements are present in the transcript.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Provider indicated need to call an ambulance for suspected anaphylaxis.
  - Patient advised to have someone remain with her until emergency services arrive.
  - Patient instructed to take available oral antihistamine immediately in the interim (agent/dose not specified).
  - Provider discussed that she may require an injection (epinephrine) in hospital.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver:
  - Mother to call emergency number 999 and state: "suspected anaphylactic reaction and they need to come straight away." (Exact instruction as given in the transcript.)
  - Remain accompanied and take antihistamine while awaiting ambulance.
  - After hospital treatment, contact the provider/clinic to arrange follow-up for possible prescription of injections (auto-injector) and further management.
- Escalation criteria / red flags (as advised):
  - Worsening breathing difficulty, throat closing sensation, voice change, progressive/worsening swelling.
- Follow-up:
  - Patient instructed to recontact the provider after hospital discharge for further management and possible provision of injections/auto-injector.
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability:
  - Not discussed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature).
  - Objective examination findings (oropharynx, airway assessment, lung auscultation).
  - Exact antihistamine agent and dose taken or available.
  - Whether intramuscular epinephrine or auto-injector is currently available to patient.
  - Details of prior severe allergic reaction (specifics of hospitalization, epinephrine administration).
  - Medication lists and dosing (salbutamol dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Provider stated they would call an ambulance, then later asked the mother to call 999 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall intelligible and adequate for clinical documentation. Some brief moments of patient distress/dizziness with short interruptions; no significant audio gaps reported.
